headline: Oil Surge and Hawkish Fed Bets Cloud Monday's Open
body_html:
Equity futures are stepping into a cautious Monday morning after Asian stocks slipped overnight as crude oil climbed more than two percent and Treasury yields pushed higher. The dual pressure of stalled US-Iran negotiations and a firmer dollar is setting a defensive tone ahead of the open, with energy costs threatening to complicate the Federal Reserve's inflation calculus just as hawkish rate-hike expectations gather momentum.

Friday's session offered a more constructive domestic picture. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners 346 to 196 across a universe of 544 names, with Semiconductors leading all sectors higher at plus 2.44 percent, followed by Homebuilders at plus 1.31 percent and Materials at plus 1.09 percent. Software was the week's notable laggard, shedding 0.82 percent, as Zscaler tumbled more than ten percent and Twilio shed nearly eight percent. On the bright side, MaxLinear surged ten percent and Veeco Instruments added 9.28 percent to pace the semiconductor rally.

This week's macro backdrop demands attention. Gold fell more than two percent on rising rate-hike bets, the dollar remains firm, and Saudi Arabia's foreign minister is in Washington for diplomatic talks. Traders should watch oil market developments and any Fed commentary closely at the open.

briefs.headline: US-Iran Impasse Keeps Oil Markets on Edge
briefs.body: Peace negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain deadlocked, sending crude prices up more than two percent. The standoff is rattling Asian equity markets and lifting the dollar, as traders price in a prolonged period of geopolitical risk premium embedded in global energy costs.

briefs.headline: Saudi Foreign Minister Lands in Washington for High-Stakes Talks
briefs.body: Saudi Arabia's top diplomat arrived in the US capital Sunday for meetings with Secretary of State Rubio. The visit comes as Middle Eastern oil exports rebounded in September, with Riyadh boosting shipments — a development that may factor into discussions about regional stability and supply commitments.

briefs.headline: Gold Retreats Sharply as Rate-Hike Expectations Intensify
briefs.body: Bullion dropped more than two percent as investors recalibrated Fed expectations in the wake of firming inflation signals tied partly to elevated energy prices. The selloff suggests safe-haven demand is being offset by the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets in a higher-rate environment.

briefs.headline: Software Sector Faces Pressure After Friday's Broad Selloff
briefs.body: The software group was Friday's worst-performing sector, declining 0.82 percent. Security and identity names bore the brunt of selling, with Zscaler off more than ten percent, Twilio down nearly eight percent, Qualys shedding 5.75 percent, and Okta falling 5.54 percent — a cluster of losses that may overhang the group at Monday's open.

briefs.headline: Iran Fuel Disruption Accelerates Electric Truck Economics in Europe
briefs.body: A diesel price spike linked to Iran-related supply concerns has pushed the operating cost of electric heavy trucks below that of diesel equivalents in several key European Union markets, according to an environmental research group. The shift could accelerate fleet electrification timelines among logistics operators across the continent.

briefs.headline: White House Dinner with Anthropic CEO Puts AI Policy in Spotlight
briefs.body: President Trump is set to host Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei for a dinner at the White House, according to Axios. The meeting underscores the administration's deepening engagement with leading artificial intelligence developers and is likely to draw attention to federal AI regulation and procurement priorities.
